data.title: Su Neden Evrensel Çözücü? İşte Açıklaması
data.description:
Su, polar bir molekül olduğu için güçlü hidrojen bağları oluşturur. Bu bağlar suyu evrensel çözücü yapar.

#shorts #bilim #günlükhayat

scenes.text: Bir damla su ne kadar gizemli
Su polar molekül yapısı sayesinde güçlü hidrojen bağları oluşturur bu da onu evrensel çözücü yapar
Su Dünya yüzeyinin yüzde yetmiş birini kaplar ve üç hâlde bulunur
Siz de suyu nasıl kullanıyorsunuz İlginç Gerçekler kanalına abone ol

reference_source.title: Water
reference_source.text: Water is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula H2O. It is a transparent, tasteless, odorless, and nearly colorless chemical substance. It is the main constituent of Earth's streams, lakes, and oceans. Water is also the fluid of all known living organisms, in which it acts as a solvent. Water, being a polar molecule, undergoes strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding which is a large contributor to its physical and chemical properties. It is vital for all known forms of life, despite not providing food energy or being an organic micronutrient. Due to its presence in all organisms, its chemical stability, its worldwide abundance, and its strong polarity relative to its small molecular size, water is often referred to as the "universal solvent". Because Earth's surface temperature and pressure is relatively close to water's triple point, water exists on Earth as a solid, a liquid, and a gas. It forms precipitation in the form of rain and aerosols in the form of fog. Clouds consist of suspended droplets of water and ice, its solid state. When finely divided, crystalline ice may precipitate in the form of snow. The gaseous state of water is steam or water vapor. Water covers about 71% of the Earth's surface, with seas and oceans making up most of the water volume (about 96.5%). Small portions of water occur as groundwater (1.7%), in the glaciers and the ice caps of Antarctica and Greenland (1.7%), and in the air as vapor, clouds (consisting of ice and liquid water suspended in air), and precipitation (0.001%).
